model.rationale: The district's fundamentals point decisively toward the Democrat after redistricting, and markets price Ben McAdams at roughly 95% while he outspends Riley Owen by more than 15-to-1. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the race stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: Any credible public polling showing a single-digit race, or a shift in the national environment, would be the first sign this is closer than fundamentals suggest.

overview:
Utah's first district is an open seat after redistricting, and its fundamentals now favor Democrats by a wide margin. Ben McAdams enters as the clear financial favorite, having raised $2.3 million and benefited from $2.7 million in outside support, while Republican Riley Owen has raised about $133 thousand with minimal cash on hand. Independent and Libertarian candidates also appear on the ballot but lack resources.

Prediction markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket price the Democrat at 94-95%, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With no public polls or expert ratings available, the forecast leans on those fundamentals and market pricing, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic win in this newly drawn seat.
